\label{lemma-compose-base-change-maps}
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X' \ar[r]_k \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y' \ar[r]^l \ar[d]_{g'} & Y \ar[d]^g \\
Z' \ar[r]^m & Z
}
$$
of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes where
both diagrams are cartesian and where $f$ and $l$
as well as $g$ and $m$ are Tor independent.
Then the maps (\ref{equation-base-change-map})
for the two squares compose to give the base
change map for the outer rectangle (see proof for a precise statement).
stage_b_review_note: At line 1020 the source has two vertically stacked Cartesian Tor-independent squares and asserts compatibility of the duality base-change maps with outer rectangle. The draft retains the stacked diagram and gives the uniquely type-correct sequential composite Lk* a_f a_g -> a_f' Ll* a_g -> a_f' a_g' Lm*, equivalent to the source's composition claim.
statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Suppose there is a vertically stacked diagram of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X'&\xrightarrow{k}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{\ell}&Y\\
g'\downarrow&&\downarrow g\\
Z'&\xrightarrow{m}&Z
\end{matrix}
\]
with both squares cartesian and pairs $(f,\ell)$ and $(g,m)$ Tor-independent. Let $a_f,a_{f'},a_g,a_{g'}$ be the right adjoints of their derived pushforwards. For each square let $\alpha$ denote the canonical duality base-change transformation $L(\text{upper-horizontal})^*a_{\text{right-vertical}}\to a_{\text{left-vertical}}L(\text{lower-horizontal})^*$ constructed as the mate of derived pushforward base change. Under identifications $a_{g\circ f}\simeq a_f a_g$ and $a_{g'\circ f'}\simeq a_{f'}a_{g'}$, the base-change map for the *outer* rectangle is precisely the composite
\[
Lk^*a_fa_g\xrightarrow{\alpha_{\rm top}\,a_g}a_{f'}L\ell^*a_g
\xrightarrow{a_{f'}\,\alpha_{\rm bottom}}a_{f'}a_{g'}Lm^*.
\]
hypotheses: Two vertically stacked cartesian qcqs Tor-independent squares.
conclusions: Duality base-change transformations for stacked vertical squares compose to the outer transformation.

\label{lemma-compose-base-change-maps-horizontal}
Consider a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X'' \ar[r]_{g'} \ar[d]_{f''} & X' \ar[r]_g \ar[d]_{f'} & X \ar[d]^f \\
Y'' \ar[r]^{h'} & Y' \ar[r]^h & Y
}
$$
of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes where
both diagrams are cartesian and where $f$ and $h$
as well as $f'$ and $h'$ are Tor independent.
Then the maps (\ref{equation-base-change-map})
for the two squares compose to give the base
change map for the outer rectangle (see proof for a precise statement).

The draft's first right-square pullback map followed by the left-square map has the correct variance and domains and preserves both Tor-independent pairs.
statement:
Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the unbounded derived category of complexes of $\mathcal O_T$-modules having quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, denote by $a_f:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the right adjoint to the derived pushforward $Rf_*$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_X(E,a_f(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*E,K)$ naturally in $E,K$, with unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to a_f Rf_*$ and counit $\operatorname{Tr}_f:Rf_*a_f\to\mathrm{id}$. This right adjoint is not in general the Grothendieck upper-shriek functor $f^!$. Suppose there are horizontally stacked cartesian squares of qcqs schemes
\[
\begin{matrix}
X''&\xrightarrow{g'}&X'&\xrightarrow{g}&X\\
f''\downarrow&&f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y''&\xrightarrow{h'}&Y'&\xrightarrow{h}&Y.
\end{matrix}
\]
Assume $(f,h)$ and $(f',h')$ are Tor-independent pairs. Let $a,a',a''$ be the right adjoints to $Rf_*,Rf'_*,Rf''_*$. For the two squares let $\alpha_{\rm right}:Lg^*a\to a'Lh^*$ and $\alpha_{\rm left}:L(g')^*a'\to a''L(h')^*$ be the canonical duality base-change transformations. Then under $L(g\circ g')^*\cong L(g')^*Lg^*$ and $L(h\circ h')^*\cong L(h')^*Lh^*$ the base-change transformation for the outer rectangle equals
\[
L(g')^*Lg^*a\xrightarrow{L(g')^*\alpha_{\rm right}}L(g')^*a'Lh^*
\xrightarrow{\alpha_{\rm left}\,Lh^*}a''L(h')^*Lh^*.
\]
hypotheses: Two horizontally composable cartesian Tor-independent qcqs squares.
conclusions: Horizontal composition of duality base-change maps equals outer rectangle base change.
